title: The Half-Built Kite
moral: Patience helps us do things properly. When we slow down and keep trying, our work can rise higher.

pages.text:
Zeeshan and his father were making a kite on the terrace.

The sky was blue, the wind was strong, and other kites were already dancing above the houses.

Zeeshan wanted his kite to fly before everyone else's.

"Let us hurry," he said.

His father smiled. "A kite made in a hurry often comes down in a hurry."

Zeeshan tried to tie the sticks quickly. The thread slipped. The paper bent.

The glue stuck more to his fingers than to the kite.

He held up his hand. "Look, Abbu. My fingers are now a family."

His father laughed and helped him wash them.

After some time, the kite was ready. It was yellow with a blue tail.

Zeeshan ran to the edge of the terrace.

"Now?" he asked.

"Check the tail," Father said.

"It is fine," Zeeshan said.

But it was not fine. One side was longer than the other.

He threw the kite into the air.

It rose for two seconds, spun around, and dropped onto the water tank.

Zeeshan stared at it.

The neighbour's little girl clapped from the next terrace. "It did a somersault!"

Zeeshan did not feel like laughing.

He wanted to tear the kite and start again.

Father climbed carefully and brought it down.

"Shall we fix it?" he asked.

Zeeshan sighed. "It will take too long."

"Good things often do," Father said.

This time, Zeeshan slowed down. He measured the tail properly. He pressed the paper gently. He waited for the glue to dry.

The sun moved lower. Many kites were already high in the sky.

At last, Father held the kite and Zeeshan ran with the string.

The yellow kite lifted.

This time, it did not spin. It climbed higher and higher until it floated above the terrace like a small piece of sunlight.

Zeeshan's face brightened.

The neighbour's little girl shouted, "Now it is flying properly!"

Zeeshan smiled. "It learned patience."

Father looked at him. "Maybe someone else did too."

The kite pulled gently against Zeeshan's hand, as if saying thank you for not giving up.
